problems.title: Leading terms of a rational sequence
problems.question: Find the intended limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}(5n+1)(4n+3)/(2n^2-9)$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The numerator is $20n^2+19n+3$. Divide by n².
steps: The quotient tends to 20/2=10.
problems.note: The printed limit label says x→∞ although the expression uses n. The numerical answer 10 uses the evident intended limit n→∞; with n fixed, the literal x-limit would simply be the unchanged expression.

problems.title: Derivative of a constant plus cosine
problems.question: For $f(x)=\sin(\pi/2)+\cos x$, find f′(π/2).
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The sine term is the constant 1, so $f\prime(x)=-\sin x$.
steps: At π/2, the sine is 1.

problems.title: Increasing interval of an exponential correction
problems.question: Find the maximal increasing interval of $f(x)=3^x-x\ln3$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: $f\prime(x)=\ln3(3^x-1)$.
steps: Since ln3>0, the derivative is positive exactly when 3ˣ>1, or x>0. It is negative for x<0.

problems.title: An oblique asymptote after cancellation
problems.question: Find the listed asymptote of $y=x^3/(x^2+9x)$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: For x≠0,−9, the expression is $x^2/(x+9)=x-9+81/(x+9)$.
steps: The final fraction tends to 0 as x→±∞, so the oblique asymptote is y=x−9. Cancellation retains the original excluded point x=0.

problems.title: Choose an ellipse directrix
problems.question: Choose a directrix of $x^2/3+y^2=2$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: Standard for m is $x^2/6+y^2/2=1$. Thus a²=6, c=2, and directrices are $x=\pm a^2/c=\pm3$.
steps: The printed choice x=−3 is one of them.

problems.title: Inflection count of a quartic
problems.question: How many inflection points has $x^4/12-5x^3/6+2x^2+7$?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The second derivative is $x^2-5x+4=(x-1)(x-4)$.
steps: Its sign changes at both simple roots 1 and 4. Each gives an inflection point.

problems.title: An exponential compared with a log product
problems.question: Solve $2^x>\log_925\cdot\log_581$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The product is $(2\ln5/2\ln3)(4\ln3/\ln5)=4$.
steps: Thus 2ˣ>2², and increasing base 2 gives x>2.

problems.title: Chain rule for a sine power
problems.question: For $f(x)=\sin^4(2x)+4x^2$, find f′(π/8).
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: $f\prime(x)=8\sin^3(2x)\cos(2x)+8x$.
steps: At x=π/8, both sine and cosine of 2x are √2/2. Their product sin³·cos is 1/4, so the first term is 2. The second is π.

problems.title: Area determines a vertical boundary
problems.question: The region bounded by y=3x²+6x, y=0, x=1, x=a has are a 50. Find a listed possible a.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: An antiderivative is $F(x)=x^3+3x^2$. For a>1 the curve is positive, so are a $F(a)-F(1)=a^3+3a^2-4$.
steps: Setting this to 50 gives a³+3a²=54. The listed a=3 satisfies 27+27=54, and the are a increases strictly for a>1.
If a is allowed left of 1, a second solution occurs with a<−2. Splitting at roots −2,0 gives are a 12−F(a), so it equals 50 when a³+3a²+38=0. This cubic has a unique root below −2.
problems.answer: Listed value: a=3. An additional negative value exists if a<1 is allowed.
problems.note: No a>1 restriction is printed. The listed positive answer 3 is valid; the full unrestricted solution also includes the unique root below −2 of a³+3a²+38=0.

problems.title: Square frustum volume from base diagonals
problems.question: A regular square frustum has space diagonal 9 and base diagonals√50,√98. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The base sides are √50/√2=5 and √98/√2=7. A space diagonal has horizontal offsets 6,6.

problems.title: Product of reciprocal-base equation roots
problems.question: Find the product of roots of $((3-\sqrt5)/2)^x+((3+\sqrt5)/2)^x=3$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The positive bases multiply to 1 and sum to 3. Set t=(3+√5)/2>1, u=tˣ.
steps: u+1/u=3 gives u²−3u+1=0, whose roots are t and 1/t. Thus x=1 or −1. Their product is −1.

problems.title: An inequality fixes the log-base direction
problems.question: Solve $\log_a(2x^2-3x-3)<\log_a(x-3)$, given that x=4 satisfies it.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: At x=4, the arguments are 17 and 1, so logₐ17<0 forces 0<a<1. The joint domain reduces to x>3.
steps: Reverse the argument inequality:2x²−3x−3>x−3, or 2x(x−2)>0. It holds for every x>3.

problems.title: Distance to either ellipse focus
problems.question: Which listed distance is possible from A=(7,0) to a focus of 16x²+25y²=400?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The ellipse is $x^2/25+y^2/16=1$, with foci(±3,0).
steps: Distances from A are 4 and 10. Of the printed choices, only 10 appears.
problems.answer: Listed distance:10. Both possible distances are 4 and 10.

problems.title: Points on opposite sides of a plane
problems.question: Which listed point pair lies on opposite sides of 2x+3y−5z+7=0, for A=(1,2,3), B=(−1,2,−3), C=(−3,1,4), D=(2,1,−1), E=(5,1,4)?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: Evaluate the signed plane expression at each point. Opposite sides require values with opposite signs.
steps: The values are A:0, B:26, C:−16, D:19, E:0. Among the listed pairs, only B, C have opposite signs. Points A, E lie on the plane rather than either open half-space.

problems.title: A constant integral with cancelling angles
problems.question: Evaluate $\int_1^3[\sin(76\pi/7)+\cos(149\pi/14)]\,dx$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: Reduce phases modulo 2π: $\sin(76\pi/7)=\sin(6\pi/7)=\sin(\pi/7)$ and $\cos(149\pi/14)=\cos(9\pi/14)=-\sin(\pi/7)$.
steps: The constant integrand is identically 0. Its integral is 0.

problems.title: Check minimum versus maximum locations
problems.question: Find a for which the minimum point of $f(x)=16^x-4^{x+1}+5$ and maximum point of $g(x)=x^3-ax^2+5$ coincide.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: $f(x)=(4^x-2)^2+1$, so its minimum abscissa is x=1/2. Cubic critical points are 0 and 2a/3, with $g\prime\prime(x)=6x-2a$.
steps: For a>0, the local maximum of g occurs at 0; its point 2a/3 is a local minimum. For a<0, the local maximum is at 2a/3<0. For a=0, the cubic has no local extremum. None can have a maximum at x=1/2.
The formal choice a=3/4 obtained from 2a/3=1/2 instead matches the cubic’s minimum location, not its maximum. Moreover the actual y-values would differ if “point” meant both coordinates.
problems.note: The listed a=3/4 reverses the cubic extremum type. The printed maximum condition is inconsistent with a positive minimum abscissa 1/2.

problems.title: Range of an exponential with bounded oscillation
problems.question: Find the range of $f(x)=4^x2^{1+\sin^2x}$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: $f(x)=2^{2x+1+\sin^2x}>0$. Its exponent has derivative 2+sin 2x≥1, so it is strictly increasing.
steps: The bounded sine-square term cannot prevent the exponent tending to −∞ as x→−∞ or+∞ as x→∞. Continuity then makes f cover every positive real value.

problems.title: A printed limit with nonzero numerator
problems.question: Evaluate the printed $\lim_{x\to0}(4e^x x-3)/(4x^2+8x)$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The numerator tends to −3, while the denominator is $4x(x+2)$ and tends to 0 with the sign of x near 0.
steps: As x→0⁺, the quotient tends to −∞. As x→0⁻, it tends to+∞. The two one-sided limits disagree.
problems.answer: The two-sided limit does not exist.
problems.note: None of the printed finite choices is correct for the displayed numerator 4eˣ·x−3. A finite value would require a change to the expression.

problems.title: Surface of a sphere from two circular sections
problems.question: Two radius 5 circles on a sphere lie in perpendicular planes and share a chord 2√2. Find sphere surface are a.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: Let equal plane distances from the sphere centre be h. Then $R^2-h^2=25$ and $R^2-2h^2=2$.
steps: Subtract to obtain h²=23 and R²=48. Sphere are a is 4πR².

problems.title: A graph’s true nearest point to a line
problems.question: Find the point on f(x)=x³−6x²+9x+3 nearest to y=−3x−7.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
steps: It attains its absolute minimum 0 where(x−2)³=−18. Thus x=2−∛18, and y=−3x−7=3∛18−13. The graph intersects the line there.

This point is not among the printed choices. If comparison is restricted to the listed points that actually belong to the graph, the closest is(−1,−13), with distance 9/√10. The stationary tangent point(2,5) has distance 18/√10 and is not a minimum.
problems.note: The printed choices omit the actual graph–line intersection. The listed tangent-parallel point(2,5) does not minimise distance.

problems.title: Minimum integral over a parameter
problems.question: Find a minimising $\int_0^1(3x^2-4ax+a^2)\,dx$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: Integrating gives $1-2a+a^2=(a-1)^2$.
steps: The square is nonnegative and vanishes at a=1.

problems.title: Rotate a parabola slice
problems.question: Rotate the region between x=1, x=4, y=0 and y²=2x around the x-axis. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: Disk volume is $V=\pi\int_1^4y^2\,dx=\pi\int_1^4 2x\,dx$.
steps: Evaluate π[x²]₁⁴=π(16−1).

problems.title: Cancellation by reflection in an integral
problems.question: Evaluate $\int_0^4[f(x)+2-f(4-x)]\,dx$, assuming f is integrable.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The substitution u=4−x gives $\int_0^4f(4-x)\,dx=\int_0^4f(u)\,du$.
steps: The two f integrals cancel. Only the constant integral∫₀⁴2dx remains.

problems.title: A line parallel to AB within a plane
problems.question: A=(1,0,3), B=(3,−2,1), C=(6,1,2). Which listed D is on x−2y+3z=10 and makes CD∥AB?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: $AB=(2,-2,-2)$. All candidates on the required line are $D=C+tAB=(6+2t,1-2t,2-2t)$.
steps: The plane expression for this entire line is 10, since the direction is parallel to the plane and C lies in it. At t=4, we obtain the listed D=(14,−7,−6), which satisfies both conditions. The other listed points are not on the line.

problems.title: A sum of nonnegative quantities
problems.question: Find 2x+3y if $2^{|x|}-\cos y+\lg(1+x^2+|y|)+\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos t\,dt=1$.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the stated conclusion follows.
formulas: The integral is 1. After cancellation, the equation is $[2^{|x|}-1]+[1-\cos y]+\lg(1+x^2+|y|)=0$.
steps: Each of the three bracketed or logarithmic terms is nonnegative. Thus each must vanish. In particular, the logarithm is 0 only if x²+|y|=0, so x=y=0. These values also make the other two terms vanish.
